decisions.text: The frontier slot's repair arms move from DeepInfra to NextBit, with the committed config deepseek-v4-pro-0813_nextbit_enabled-false, for the dev re-run and the test round. Every other slot is unchanged, and the counted first turns stay the answers DeepInfra served.

The dev frontier round is re-run on NextBit before the test round, as new runs whose ids carry the tag nb after the arm tag. The owner was told and did not object; the owner's paid dev command is the confirmation.
On NextBit an arm run keeps the protocol's outage rule: one re-run from scratch, -nb-r2 on dev and -r2 on test. A second outage is not run, and no arm moves again.
The test frontier arms keep their registered ids, which no request has used.

rejected.why: its endpoint lists no seed, and require_parameters is true, so a seeded request cannot route to it

the 198 attempts record no cause, and the one later HTTP 429 body the owner saw names a shared pool (engine_overloaded, upstream_provider_shared_pool), which gives no bound on recovery; one later HTTP 200 from that pool did not show it usable

rejected.option: reporting the frontier round not run
rejected.why: it would leave the frontier slot without a repair measurement while its registered fallback config, with the same fp8 label and seed support, is committed

unchanged: the counted first turns: the dev and test passes' answers that DeepInfra served

every other setting and call option of the frontier arm runs: model, reasoning switch, temperature 0, seed 17, max_output_tokens 2048, JSON mode, a 120 s timeout, require_parameters true, allow_fallbacks false, --gate-first, --max-attempts 3 and --min-interval-seconds 1.0
the frontier caps: 0.20 USD on dev and 0.50 USD on test
every other model's arm runs, configs and caps
the 108 registered arm run ids, the registry's rows and statuses, and the baseline test passes
the repair plans and their triggered items
why: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813 got no answer on its DeepInfra-pinned route (provider order deepinfra, allow_fallbacks false) in any of the 198 attempts of its three dev arm runs and their -r2 re-runs, sent between 02:23 and 02:41 UTC: all were HTTP 429 and nothing was charged. The run records keep only the error code 429 and no served provider. One request the owner sent afterwards got an HTTP 429 whose body names engine_overloaded and upstream_provider_shared_pool. Its test baseline had already met 776 HTTP 429 on the same route, 754 of them before an item's last attempt. NextBit is the bake-off note's listed frontier fallback, committed in de05cad: the same fp8 label, seed supported, and the same settings but provider order and prices. Decided with 0 frontier repair answers on dev and no test repair request sent.
